phrase: A technology company stopped accepting bug reports because so many were written by AI and wrong. A government unveiled a new task force to manage the AI it renamed.
phraseAlternatives: So many AI-written bug reports arrived that a company just turned off the intake. One government renamed its AI problem instead of solving it.
A company stopped reading bug reports because AI kept writing broken ones. A government, meanwhile, gave its AI problem a brand-new name.
Fake AI bug reports flooded a company until it gave up reading them. A government chose a bigger name for the same old AI problem.
alt: A stacked two-panel print: on top, a tired worker swings a large stamp down onto a paper labeled "Rejected" as more papers with tiny robot heads overflow a tray; below, a proud painter on a ladder repaints a plain government building's sign, adding a longer, fancier label reading "New Name".

brief.concept: Two institutions face the same AI headache and choose two kinds of avoidance: one stops looking, the other just renames it.
brief.metaphor: Stamping a flood of fake reports 'rejected' and repainting a sign with a fancier label are both ways of dodging the real fix.

brief.composition: Two side-by-side panels on one card, separated by a thin line. Left panel: a worker stands over an overflowing inbox tray, bringing a large stamp down on a paper; more papers marked with tiny robot heads spill out of the tray. Right panel: a sign painter on a short ladder repaints a plain government building's sign, replacing a short label with a longer, squiggly, fancier-looking label mid brush-stroke. Flat shapes, one accent ink color per panel, minimal text.
